answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit slashed on proven misbehavior, like a cedar stake anchoring a young tree: cheap to plant once, costly to uproot in bulk. An atlas of reputation records verified work over time, so a fresh identity starts at its nadir with no history and no trust. An attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand deposits, endure the same slow reputation climb, and risk losing every stake when one fraud is proved, making mass fakery costlier than the influence it buys.
